about.title: Saratoga Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Saratoga's mix of small commercial centers, hillside properties, and busy corridors like Saratoga Sunnyvale Road and Saratoga Los Gatos Road means workplace injuries here often involve more than just an employer. Delivery drivers, landscapers, contractors, and retail employees can be hurt not only by workplace hazards but by negligent third parties — another driver, a subcontractor, or defective equipment. California generally requires injured workers to pursue workers' compensation first, since it's usually the exclusive remedy against an employer. But when someone outside the employment relationship contributes to the injury, a separate claim may be possible. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee itself; we simply connect injured workers in Saratoga with an independent attorney who can look at the full picture, explain your options clearly, and help you understand whether a workers' comp claim, a third-party claim, or both may apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: While workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still be liable separately.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires injuries to be reported to your employer within 30 days, so timing your claim correctly can protect your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: If you're worried about reporting an injury, California law prohibits employer retaliation for filing a workers' comp claim.

items.question: Can I file a claim if I was hurt while driving for work near SR-85 or Saratoga Avenue?
items.answer: Possibly. If another driver caused the crash while you were performing work duties, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. An independent attorney can help sort out which claims apply and how they interact.

items.question: What if my employer doesn't have workers' comp insurance?
items.answer: California employers are generally required to carry workers' comp coverage, but if yours doesn't, you may have additional legal options. An attorney can explain what remedies exist in that situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party injury claim in California?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. Workers' comp reporting has its own shorter 30-day window, so it's important not to delay either process.
